Yeasts are unicellular eukaryotic fungi that reproduce via budding or fission, with over 1,500 known species constituting about 1% of all fungi. They exhibit remarkable diversity in size, form, and lifestyle, ranging from species that form multicellular structures to opportunistic pathogens like Candida albicans. The species Saccharomyces cerevisiae is pivotal for fermentation in baking and brewing and serves as a fundamental model organism in biological research. Yeasts do not form a single phylogenetic group but are found across two fungal phyla, with their history of human use documented back thousands of years. They are chemoorganotrophs that grow on organic compounds, with growth conditions varying widely among species.
